claims.text: Mixed-metal high-entropy compositions induce local electronic heterogeneity.
Mixed-metal high-entropy compositions induce local structural heterogeneity, including strain near active sites.
The electronic and structural heterogeneity tunes the adsorption energies or interaction strengths of reaction intermediates.
High-entropy catalysts can exhibit greater catalytic activity than corresponding single-metal, binary, or lower-entropy catalysts.
High-entropy catalysts can exhibit improved desired-product selectivity relative to single- or binary-metal catalysts.
High-entropy catalysts can exhibit greater operational durability than lower-entropy catalysts.
LaCr0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Co0.2Ni0.2O3-δ can be prepared as an epitaxial catalyst layer with a defined (001) facet.
PtPdCoCuNi can be prepared as supported high-entropy alloy nanoparticles for nitrobenzene hydrogenation.
The proposed catalyst series can maintain uniform morphology and crystallographic facets while composition is varied from single-metal to high-entropy formulations.
Interactions among different transition-metal sites cause charge redistribution.
Interactions among different transition-metal sites produce shifts in metal valence states.
The simultaneous presence of multiple metals creates a distribution of active sites with distinct local electronic environments.
This active-site heterogeneity enables optimal OH* or H* binding by breaking conventional adsorption-energy scaling relationships.
Tuned intermediate binding lowers energy barriers for key catalytic steps.
The heterogeneous sites prevent intermediate overbinding that would otherwise cause side reactions or catalyst deactivation.
The high-entropy perovskite should produce higher catalytic current than its single-B-site parents at a fixed OER overpotential.
In situ XPS or APXPS should reveal dynamic, synergistic valence changes of mixed metals during catalysis.
Single-B-site perovskites exhibit conventional volcano-type OER activity trends.
The hypothesis should apply to reactions such as OER and selective hydrogenation when intermediate adsorption energetics govern the rate.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when catalysis is controlled solely by bulk properties or when surface electronic effects are minimal.

contradictions.description: The central hypothesis asserts enhancement of activity, selectivity, and durability together, whereas the predicted outcome only requires improvement in one or more of these properties ('and/or').

The uncertainty field allows strain rather than charge redistribution to be the principal mediator, but the falsification rule treats absence of synergistic valence modification and charge redistribution as sufficient to falsify the entire hypothesis. A strain-mediated performance enhancement could therefore satisfy the stated mechanism while triggering falsification.
